stem: At which site in Greece is the Olympic flame lit, using a curved mirror to focus the Sun's rays?
explanation: The ceremony takes place among the ruins of the Temple of Hera. A torch relay then carries the flame to the host city, a custom that began with the 1936 Berlin Games.

claims.text: The Olympic flame is lit at ancient Olympia in Greece, with a parabolic mirror focusing sunlight.
The Olympic flame is not lit on Mount Olympus, in Athens or at Delphi.
The lighting ceremony is held at the Temple of Hera in Olympia.
The Olympic torch relay from Olympia to the host city was first held for the 1936 Berlin Olympics.

writerNotes: Subtopic: Olympic history. Easy. lint: clean. claims: four; c4 high (the first relay). datasets: olympic-editions confirms that Berlin hosted the 1936 Summer Games (edition_id 11) but says nothing of the relay, so c4 needs web evidence (the IOC's Olympic flame page or Britannica). rivalTest: Mount Olympus is the planted confusion (the gods' mountain, which gave Olympia nothing but a similar name); Athens hosted 1896 and 2004 and hands the flame over in the Panathenaic Stadium, so it tempts; Delphi is another famous ancient site. Argued against the key: the flame passes through Athens after the lighting, but it is lit at Olympia. Every Olympic flame since 1936, Summer and Winter, has been lit there, so the stem's present tense holds. volatility: evergreen. regional: the flame ceremony is broadcast worldwide. style: Oxford spelling, explanation of 31 words. myths: screened; the cut item p.sport.0114 (a torch-relay myth) states the relay is not ancient, which agrees with c4. mystery and encore: not applicable. doubts: none.
